h: Shabbos Restores the Double Crown and Its Blessings

p: 'We will do' before 'We will hear,' etc.,
they tied to each two crowns,
and one corresponding to 'We will hear.'"
And in the Pesikta it is stated:
one hundred twenty myriads of ministering angels:
one ties on him a crown,
and one girds him with his weapon.
That is, the crown corresponds to "We will hear,"
and it is called a crown,
corresponding to the tefillin of the head,
which correspond to the neshamah in the brain;
and it is a crown on the head.
these are the tefillin of the head."
And "yekar" is the aspect of the primordial light,
כָּל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ (אִיּוֹב כח, י)
רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כּוּלֵּי
"the eye of Rabbi Akiva saw," etc.
"And one girds him with his weapon":
the belt corresponds to "We will do,"
and it corresponds to the tefillin of the arm,
שֶׁכָּל הַפְּעוּלּוֹת מְכוּנּוֹת עַל שֵׁם הַיָּדַיִם
for all actions are named after the hands;
and it corresponds to the heart,
to subjugate the desires and thoughts of our heart
to His service, blessed be His Name.
And in the Gemara they said two crowns,
for from the tefillin of the arm too,
at the time of Mattan Torah,
as it is written, "With the crown with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding"
when Yisrael crowned HaKadosh Baruch Hu
with the crowns of "We will do" and "We will hear";
and then Yisrael too were crowned
You have made Me a single entity in the world,
as it says, etc., 'Hashem is One';
a single entity in the world, etc.:
and only the crown of "We will hear" remained.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
And about this the Pesikta mentioned above says,
And the crowns are from the primordial light,
"And Moshe merited all of them and took them,
for next to it is written,
וּמֹשֶׁה יִקַּח אֶת הָאוֹהֶל (שְׁמוֹת לג, ז)
מִלְּשׁוֹן בְּהִלּוֹ נֵרוֹ עַל רֹאשִׁי (אִיּוֹב כט, ג)
from the expression "when His lamp shone over my head" (Iyov 29:3).
And this is the primordial light,
above the head, as is known.
And it is stated in the Pri Etz Chaim
that on Shabbos Moshe Rabbeinu returns
And this is what we say beforehand:
the aspect of the primordial light,
which is like a crown upon the head,
"when His lamp shone over my head."
And here we say, "Great joy will come,
for on weekdays only one crown remains,
from the tefillin of the head,
but on Shabbos there are both crowns:
as is written, the Torah was given on Shabbos,
and Shabbos should be made entirely Torah
and the crown of "We will do,"
as is written in the Mechilta:
"'Who keeps the Shabbos from profaning it
וְשׁוֹמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע (יְשַׁעְיָה נו, ב)
and keeps his hand from doing any evil' (Yeshayahu 56:2):
And this is "And upon one, a double
that on Shabbos both crowns come,
which are the aspect of the primordial light.
And on Shabbos tefillin are not needed,
for it is itself a sign (Eruvin 96a);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהוֹלְכִין כָּל הַמֵּעֵת לְעֵת בִּתְפִילִּין
and it is as though one goes the entire day and night in tefillin,
which on weekdays is not the time for tefillin,
since then is not a time of activity;
but on Shabbos, even at night,
it is as if one goes in tefillin,
and we merit the two crowns,
the crown of "We will do" and the crown of "We will hear."
And this is "And upon one, a double
for the root of all blessings
"and the matter does not depend on merit
and in the holy Zohar (end of Parshas Acharei)
it is that this refers to the "mazal" above,
And on Shabbos, when "light will reach her,"
that is, from the primordial light,
from which the crowns come, as mentioned above;
it reckons "Let there be light" as the first utterance,
which is the most hidden of all, beyond all thought.
And when there is a revelation of Atika,
for the essence of the blessings,
their intent, is in matters of the soul,
that is, increase of light and revelation and holiness;
and automatically there branch out from it
the blessing of life, children and sustenance,
The blessing of the fish corresponds to life,
for with the fish we find for the first time
the word "life" mentioned in the Torah:
And the blessing of man, "Be fruitful and multiply,"
it is stated (Bereishis Rabbah, beginning of chapter 11, 11:1):
בִּרְכַּת ה׳ הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר (מִשְׁלֵי י, כב)
"for all the blessings above and below
depend on the seventh day," etc.,
with which they are blessed on the seventh day," etc.;
